title: Transformers — Working Principle & Turns Ratio
subtitle: A transformer is the most elegant device in electrical engineering — no moving parts, over 98% efficiency. The turns ratio unlocks everything. It works ONLY on AC: DC gives constant flux → dφ/dt=0 → zero secondary EMF.

topics.title: Working Principle, Turns Ratio & Referred Impedance

subtopics.title: Working Principle, Turns Ratio & Referred Impedance

content.text: AC in primary → changing flux in core → changing flux links secondary → EMF induced. No direct electrical connection. Only works on AC because steady DC gives constant flux (dφ/dt=0) → no induced EMF → primary burns.
Turns ratio k = N₁/N₂ = E₁/E₂ = V₁/V₂. Current transforms inversely: I₁/I₂ = N₂/N₁ = 1/k. Power conserved: V₁I₁ = V₂I₂ (ideal).
Referred impedance: Z₂' = k²×Z₂ (secondary → primary). Z₁' = Z₁/k² (primary → secondary). Moving to HV side: multiply by k². Moving to LV side: divide by k².
k > 1 → step-down · k < 1 → step-up Core type: flux passes through one limb, windings on same limb Shell type: flux divides, windings surrounded by core — better for LV high current

Common mistake — Moving LV→HV: multiply by k². Moving HV→LV: divide by k². Students multiply in both directions. Also never say "transformer works on DC if powerful enough" — DC transformers do not exist.
